answer: A practical defence is to make identity expensive to fake but cheap to prove: require each agent to stake a modest bond and build a verifiable history of useful work, so a sybil swarm cannot simply clone itself. Like water carving a karst landscape, trust should form slowly through real interaction, not appear overnight. A reputation prism that splits an agent record into separate facets - reliability, honesty, and stake - makes cheap copies stand out, while a cedar-like root of long-term, cross-checked attestations anchors genuine agents. Fakes then cost more to maintain than they can earn.
